previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for worsening right-sided headache and eye pain, found to have a new nasopharyngeal mass on MRI, raising concern for recurrent lymphoma given her history of DLBCL. She also had severe sinusitis with purulent drainage. A biopsy was performed, revealing CD30-positive cells of uncertain origin, with cultures growing Streptococcus pneumoniae and MRSA. She was treated with intravenous vancomycin after discontinuing Levaquin due to resistance. Her symptoms improved, and repeat imaging showed slight improvement in sinus disease but a stable nasopharyngeal mass. Bone marrow biopsy was performed but results were pending at discharge. She completed a week of inpatient antibiotics and was discharged on a 14-day course of oral vancomycin with follow-up arranged in oncology, ENT, and infectious disease. Chronic conditions including CVID, diabetes, and chronic pain were managed throughout.

radiology_notes.text:
LEFT SHOULDER RADIOGRAPH PERFORMED ON ___.

___.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Possible recurrence of lymphoma with new onset left
shoulder pain.

FINDINGS:  Three views of the left shoulder were provided, demonstrating no
acute fracture or dislocation.  No significant degenerative disease is seen. 
Soft tissues appear normal.

IMPRESSION:  Unremarkable radiographs of the left shoulder.

HISTORY:  B-cell lymphoma and shoulder pain.  Please evaluate for shoulder
pathology.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial, coronal and sagittal T1, T2 and proton density weighted
images were obtained on a 1.5T magnet through the left shoulder without
administration of intravenous contrast.  Motion degraded images were repeated.

COMPARISON:  Radiographs of the left shoulder from ___.

FINDINGS:

The supraspinatus, infraspinatus, subscapularis and teres minor muscles are
normal in signal intensity and morphology. 

The subscapularis tendon shows mild thickening with increased signal within it
but no discrete tear is noted.  The teres minor and infra-spinatus tendon are
normal in signal intensity and morphology.  There is mild fraying on the
bursal surface of the supraspinatus tendon. 

Trace fluid is noted in the subacromial/subdeltoid bursa.  There is mild joint
space narrowing with superior and inferior osteophytic spurring consistent
with mild acromioclavicular osteoarthritis. 

There is loss of normal fat signal on T1 and T2 weighted images in the rotator
interval. This is associated with thickening of the coracohumeral ligament and
inferior glenohumeral ligament. 

The biceps tendon is intact.  

The anteroinferior glenoid labrum is not well seen but the remaining labrum
appears intact. The glenohumeral cartilage is normal in signal intensity and
morphology. 

No lymphadenopathy is present.  The marrow signal is normal.

IMPRESSION:

1. Loss of normal fat signal in the rotator interval with thickening of the
coracohumeral and inferior glenohumeral ligament consistent with adhesive
capsulitis.

2. Tendinosis of the subscapularis and supraspinatus tendons. 

3. Mild acromioclavicular osteoarthritis.
